title: Orbital Hold: Last Beacon
premise: A stationary orbital beacon platform is under constant assault by an incoming swarm, and the player must defend the central core with a touch-aimed turret while deploying charge-powered support tools.
interaction_model: Real-time touch/mouse aiming and hold-to-fire turret defense combined with drag-and-drop upgrade card placement onto either the center core or the perimeter barricade ring.
objective: Survive as long as possible, destroy incoming enemies, maintain the hull of the central beacon, and manage the perimeter defenses through timely card-based upgrades.
progression: Enemy spawn pressure increases over time, enemy health and speed scale upward by sector/wave, score rises by kills, and every 50 kills the threat band advances. Kills also fill a charge meter that periodically generates random upgrade cards, creating a cyclical combat-and-support progression loop.
theme: Sci-fi last-stand orbital defense with neon HUD styling, beacon imagery, and a lone command-post-under-siege fantasy.
mood: Tense, arcade-like, reactive, and heroic, with bright neon feedback and escalating danger.
likely_audience: players who enjoy compact arcade survival games
wave defense players who like light tactical ability management
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a stationary wave-defense shooter with touch aiming and card-based support abilities.
Moderate confidence on fiction wording because the code uses internal names like 'zombies' while the UI presents enemies as drones and the setting as orbital sci-fi defense.
High confidence that barricade preservation and upgrade timing are central to intended play.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen sci-fi survival defense game called 'Orbital Hold: Last Beacon' where the player controls a stationary central beacon turret in the middle of the screen and must survive endless waves of incoming swarm enemies approaching from all directions. Use a full-screen canvas with a futuristic neon HUD, glassy overlay panels, scanline styling, and responsive mobile-first layout. The core interaction should be touch or mouse based: the player presses and drags anywhere on the arena to aim the turret, and while holding input the turret continuously auto-fires toward the pointer. Enemies spawn outside the visible play field, move inward toward the center, and either attack a circular ring of six perimeter defense panels first or damage the central hull if they break through. Kills should increase score, fill a charge meter, and every full charge should generate a random draggable ability card in a bottom dock with room for three cards. Cards must be dragged onto valid zones: center-target cards affect the core or turret, while perimeter-target cards affect the barricade ring; invalid drops should fail and keep the card. Include four signature abilities: a repair card that restores damaged or destroyed panels, a rapid-fire overdrive card that boosts firing speed temporarily, an ion burst that stuns and damages all active enemies, and an alloy reinforce card that upgrades the entire perimeter into stronger metal panels. Scale pressure over time by increasing enemy health, speed, and spawn rate, and advance the displayed threat sector every 50 kills. Present the action with muzzle flashes, shell casings, particles, screen shake, low-health vignette, strong audio feedback, and start/game-over overlays. The overall feel should be a compact arcade holdout game that blends turret shooter intensity with light drag-and-drop tactical support decisions.
